title: Orchestrated Terraform remediation recipes and stepwise runbooks for VPC probe regressions
creator: Carlos Mendes
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a set of deterministic remediation recipes and stepwise runbooks to automatically detect and remediate the top recurring Private (VPC) health-check failures we see in customer deployments. The goal is to provide safe, auditable Terraform-driven actions (and fallbacks) that can be executed by the remediation controller with minimal blast radius and clear human escalation paths.

Scope (what we will deliver):
- A catalog of failure archetypes with detection rules and metrics (probe timeout spikes, repeated probe 502/504, Instance Metadata timeout, DNS resolution failures, kernel driver mismatch).
- Terraform module usage recommendations and small tfmodule wrappers that the remediation controller can invoke (recreate node, refresh launch template, reconcile security groups, replace broken ENIs).
- Automated preflight checks and canary execution patterns (dry-run plan, plan diff thresholding, canary apply to 1-2 nodes, monitoring probes for 10m).
- Runbook artifacts: human-readable step-by-step for oncall, and machine-readable remediation recipes consumed by the controller.
- Safety and audit controls: approval gates for >30% capacity changes, immutable audit event generation (GitHub PR + run logs), and automatic rollback criteria (latency or error regression metrics).

Failure modes covered (representative):
1) Control-plane probe flapping due to stale iptables / kernel module mismatch on private nodes. Detection: node liveness probe error rate > 5% for 3m and kernel_version deviates from fleet modal value. Remediation recipe: cordon -> create replacement node via terraform module.private_node_pool.replace(1) -> wait for readiness -> drain old node -> decommission old instance.
2) VPC DNS resolution errors (dnsmasq / resolv.conf corruption) causing model container startup failures. Detection: resolver lookup latency > 200ms and container start failures correlated to dns failures. Remediation recipe: trigger node restart for affected AZs; if restart fails, force recreate ENI using terraform module.vpc.eni_recreate(target_enis).
3) Security group regression (ingress rule accidentally removed during customer-managed IaC drift). Detection: probe failures with connection resets, drift detected by terraform plan showing rule removal. Remediation recipe: apply terraform plan to reintroduce required SG rules; if plan diff touches > 5 SG rules, escalate for manual approval.
4) Volume/FS mount corruption (EBS detach/attach race). Detection: repeated mount errors in node logs and kubelet crashloop. Remediation: provision replacement node and remap PV to new node with terraform resource replacement for instance_id.
5) Certificate expiry for internal agent->controlplane mTLS. Detection: cert_ttl < 72h for > 1 node or TLS handshake failures in logs. Remediation: rotate certs via terraform module.kms_cert_rotate + background rolling restart; block automated if CA rotation required (manual).

Implementation notes (engineering decisions and tradeoffs):
- Use Terraform as the source of truth for remediations that change infra (create/replace/taint resources). Rationale: consistent with customers' IaC mindset and audit trail via terraform plan/apply. Tradeoff: Terraform operations can be slow; mitigate with targeted resource applies and parallelism defaults.
- Remediation controller will prefer non-invasive actions first (restart, cordon/drain), then Terraform-driven replacements. This reduces accidental large-scale churn.
- For safety, all automated terraform applies default to a reviewable PR flow for production namespaces unless the outage crosses an automated severity threshold (SLO breach + customer impact high) — in which case the controller can run apply with escalation notifications.
- Avoid automatic changes that modify customer-managed network constructs without explicit allowlist for each customer.

Runbook structure (deliverables):
- Human-run runbook steps (Oncall Quick Actions) with exact commands for debugging and for invoking the remediation controller.
- Machine-run remediation recipe YAMLs that map detection -> preflight checks -> terraform target apply -> post-validation -> rollback.
- Example terraform invocation snippets and templates for the controller.

Operational validation and testing plan:
- Staging harness: scripted fault injection for each failure mode (iptables corruption, DNS drop, SG deletion, EBS detach) deployed against a dedicated Private staging cluster.
- Canary policy: apply to 1-2 nodes in a non-prod AZ, monitor control-plane probe metrics + model inference latency for 10-15m.
- Integration tests: CI job that asserts plan diffs are idempotent and that applying recipes results in green healthchecks.
- Postmortem loop: add automated ticket generation if remediation fires + fails, include run logs and terraform plans.

Audit and observability outputs to ship:
- Run-level artifacts: terraform plan diff, apply output, controller logs, CloudTrail/GCP audit entries, and Prometheus snapshot before/after.
- Dashboard: per-remediation timeline and success rate, remediation duration histogram, and false positive rate.

Backwards compatibility: all remediation recipes must support older TF module versions (>= v0.7.0) used in customer private templates. We'll include translation wrappers to map older module inputs to new module signatures.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog of >=5 failure archetypes with detection rules and automated recipes written
Terraform wrapper modules implemented and merged to repo private-terraform-modules v1.3
Remediation controller accepts YAML recipe and can perform dry-run plan and a canary apply in staging
End-to-end staging tests for each failure mode pass in CI and produce reproducible logs
Safety gates implemented: PR flow for production, >30% change requires manual approval, audit logs emitted
